title: Audit retention guardrails Terraform module for private VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Goal: Ship a reusable Terraform module that codifies audit log guardrails for private VPC deployments. The module will provision cross-account CloudTrail delivery, S3 buckets with lifecycle policies (including archival to Glacier Deep Archive), KMS-backed encryption, OpenSearch index lifecycle management (rollover/delete), and a lightweight healthcheck so platform teams can detect retention or ingestion regressions. It must be composable for both Hosted Private and on-prem templates and support zero-downtime upgrades for existing customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Terraform module exposes stable variables for account ids, kms_key_arn, retention_days, glacier_transition_days, opensearch_policy_name and supports invocation in cross-account scenarios. 2) By default the module creates an S3 bucket encrypted with supplied KMS key, CloudTrail configured to deliver both management and S3 data events, and S3 lifecycle rules: transition to Glacier after X days (configurable), noncurrent delete after Y days. 3) OpenSearch ILM templates created for log indices: hot-warm-rollover + delete policy matching retention_days. 4) Healthcheck Lambda + CloudWatch metric that emits 'audit_pipeline_ok' and a dashboard tile. 5) Module has a migration plan and CI test that runs plan/apply in a sandbox and validates artifacts and metrics.
design_summary: We will split responsibilities across three sub-resources inside the module: s3 + lifecycle + kms binding (bucket.tf), cloudtrail configuration and cross-account IAM (cloudtrail.tf), opensearch ILM + role bindings (opensearch.tf). A small 'ops' submodule will deploy a Lambda (Python) that runs weekly asserts: checks last-delivery timestamp in S3, counts recent indices in OpenSearch, verifies KMS key policy matches expected ARNs, and publishes a CloudWatch metric. The module will be parameterized for 'legacy_mode' to enable a compatibility path for existing buckets (skip bucket rename, add lifecycle via separate resource). All resources will use tags and a module-level naming prefix.
terraform_interface: Variables: name_prefix (string), environment (string), cloudtrail_account_id (string), delivering_account_id (string), kms_key_arn (string), retention_days (integer), glacier_transition_days (integer), opensearch_endpoint (string), opensearch_policy_name (string), legacy_mode (bool as string 'true'/'false'), force_destroy_bucket (string). Outputs: s3_bucket_arn, cloudtrail_id, opensearch_ilm_id, healthcheck_lambda_arn. Module supports providers map to allow multi-account apply via Terragrunt or root-level provider aliasing.
upgrade_migration_plan: - Detect existing buckets (by naming convention) and run a dry-run to collect current lifecycle rules. - Create new lifecycle rules as separate resource where possible to avoid replacing buckets. - For customers who cannot accept in-place rule changes, provide a documented two-step migration: (1) create new bucket and update CloudTrail to deliver to new bucket during maintenance window, (2) copy/verify historical objects to new bucket with verification checksums, (3) update references and deprecate old bucket. - Use Terraform 1.5 compatible code and add migration helper script (go/python) to produce 'state move' steps for provider-level renames. - Add automated plan-time checks in CI to detect destructive diffs and block merges unless approved by SRE-owner label.
healthchecks_and_alerting: Healthcheck Lambda schedule (weekly) validates: last S3 delivery object timestamp < max_age (configurable), OpenSearch index count change in expected range, CloudTrail status is 'Logging' for trail, KMS key policy contains expected ARN set. Lambda writes metrics to a CloudWatch namespace 'Redwood/AuditPipeline' with dimensions {environment,name_prefix}. We will add two alarms: 'audit_pipeline_delivery_delay' (threshold > 48 hours) -> PagerDuty, and 'audit_pipeline_missing_ilm' -> Slack channel #infra-ops. Dashboard panels: recent S3 delivery, average index size, ILM phase counts.
test_plan: - Unit: terraform validate/tfmt + terratest (Go) to assert resources are created with expected attributes. - Integration: spin up in sandbox AWS account (isolated terraform state) and run post-deploy verification: list bucket objects, query opensearch for index templates, evaluate ILM policy steps. - Regression: run against a synthetic 'legacy' stack to ensure legacy_mode avoids bucket replacement. - CI gating: require a successful integration run for PR merge. - Smoke: small log injection to CloudTrail (simulate S3 object put event) and verify delivery and 'audit_pipeline_ok' metric emission.
rollout_and_monitoring: Initial rollout: enable module in sandbox and one pilot customer VPC. Monitor for two weeks: metrics, retention enforcement, billing delta on S3/Glacier. Provide a rollback plan: toggle CloudTrail delivery back to previous bucket and remove new lifecycle rules. After pilot success, gradually enable across Dedicated clusters with a canary of 10% then 50% then full. Update Console docs and Console UI 'private deployment' checklist to include required KMS permissions and IAM roles.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Lifecycle change inadvertently deletes data. Mitigation: default to conservative retention (retain >=90 days) and require explicit opt-in lower retention. Risk: KMS key policy conflicts across accounts. Mitigation: support customer-supplied key and verify policy via healthcheck; provide templated policy snippets. Risk: CloudTrail cross-account permission errors. Mitigation: CI integration tests include cross-account assume-role checks and we will provide clear operator runbook.
